{{short description|American chemist}}
'''Norman Bernard Larsen''' (1923—1970)<ref name=obit/> was an American industrial [[chemist]].

==Biography==
He was born in [[Chicago]].<ref name=Engstrand2014/>

Larsen is sometimes credited with inventing the [[WD-40]] formula in 1953 but this is not certain.  The WD-40 company website and other books and newspapers credit him<ref>{{cite web|title=WD-40 History - History and Timeline|url=https://wd40.com/cool-stuff/history|publisher=WD-40 Company|access-date=10 April 2017|language=en}}</ref><ref name="Mercer2011">{{cite book|author=Bobby Mercer|title=ManVentions: From Cruise Control to Cordless Drills - Inventions Men Can't Live Without|url=https://archive.org/details/manventionsfromc0000merc|url-access=registration|access-date=June 28, 2013|date=March 18, 2011 |publisher=Adams Media |isbn=978-1-4405-1075-5 |pages=[https://archive.org/details/manventionsfromc0000merc/page/181 181]–}}</ref><ref name=BarryObit>{{cite news|last1=Martin|first1=Douglas|title=Obituary: John Barry, Popularizer of WD-40, Dies at 84|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2009/07/22/business/22barry1.html|work=The New York Times|date=22 July 2009}}</ref> but according to [[Iris Engstrand]], a historian of San Diego and California at the [[University of San Diego]], it was actually Iver Norman Lawson (also an engineer born in Chicago at around the same time as Norm Larsen), and the names became confused over time.<ref name=Engstrand2014>{{cite journal|last1=Engstrand|first1=Iris H.W.|title=WD-40: San Diego's Marketing Miracle|journal=The Journal of San Diego History|date=Fall 2014|volume=60|issue=4|pages=253–270|url=http://www.sandiegohistory.org/sites/default/files/journal/v60-4/v60-4engstrand.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222232703/https://sandiegohistory.org/sites/default/files/journal/v60-4/v60-4engstrand.pdf |archive-date=2015-12-22}}</ref>  The formula was kept as a [[trade secret]], so no patent was ever filed listing inventors.<ref name=BarryObit/>

Larsen left the Rocket Chemical Company (the original producers of WD-40) in 1958 after a verbal agreement between Rocket and a distributor fell apart; the distributor set up [[CRC Industries]] in Philadelphia to directly compete with Rocket and Larsen left to lead it.<ref name=CRCstory>{{cite web|title=The CRC Story|url=http://www.crcindustries.com/files/thecrcstory.pdf|publisher=CRC Industries|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060504181854/http://www.crcindustries.com/files/thecrcstory.pdf|archive-date=4 May 2006|url-status=dead}}</ref> CRC was originally called Corrosion Reaction Consultants, Inc.<ref>{{cite book|title=Industrial Research Laboratories of the United States|date=1960|publisher=National Academies|page=129|edition=10th|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=pzgrAAAAYAAJ&pg=PA129|language=en}}</ref> Its first product was called CRC [[Corrosion inhibitor|Corrosion Inhibitor]], also called 5–56.<ref name=CRCstory/>

By 1968 Larsen had left CRC and had founded a company called Surcon, Inc. headquartered in Collegeville, PA, which also had developed a chemical anti-corrosion formula eventually called "Free 'n Kleen"; the company used it to remove corrosion from the wreck of a Spanish galleon found off the Florida coast.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Dougherty|first1=Joseph E.|title=Company Restoring Pieces of Wrecked Spanish Ship|url=https://newspaperarchive.com/hanover-evening-sun-dec-05-1968-p-25/|work=Hanover Evening Sun via NewspaperArchive|date=5 December 1968|page=25|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Surcon Inc Manufacturers of Free 'n Kleen Products|url=https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/83689539/|work=Pottstown Mercury from Pottstown, Pennsylvania via Newspapers.com|date=15 November 1969|page=55|language=en}}</ref>  By 1970 the product was being used by [[Sikorsky Aircraft]] Corp in its helicopters and was also used by the military to keep machine guns working.<ref name=obit/>

Larsen died in December 1970 at home at the age of 47, of an apparent heart attack.<ref name=obit>{{cite news|title=Norman B. Larsen, 47, Surcon President Dies|url=https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/42383146/|work=Pottstown Mercury from Pottstown, Pennsylvania via Newspapers.com|date=4 December 1970|page=2|language=en}}</ref>
